criterion.text: Given all but one player have marked ready, when the room enters the holdout state, then the unready player sees a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the start countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while they remain unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the start countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. If the room has exactly two players, the holdout is not removed and the lobby continues waiting; the countdown does not begin until both are ready.

Given the game start countdown has not begun, when no player/observer membership or ready-state change occurs for 30 seconds, then the game prompts all players once for that room version to mark themselves ready; any membership or ready-state change resets the interval.

Idle prompt and readiness races: The 30-second interval resets on player/observer membership or ready-state changes. Prompt once per unchanged aggregate version. Deadlines carry the expected version; stale jobs are no-ops.

A disconnect must not corrupt accepted scores or duplicate a submission. Reconnecting players retain membership for a two-minute grace interval; after it expires the room applies the normal departure rules. Client retries reuse the original command ID.

Room code, reconnect, creator departure: Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code. Codes remain valid while the room is active and expire on close; empty rooms close after 30 minutes. Reconnect retains membership for a two-minute grace interval. Creator departure grants no special authority; remaining players retain control. Invalid/expired codes return the same generic not-found response; limit code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

findings.finding: Silent waiting-member expiry is45seconds detection plus120seconds grace,165seconds since original lastSeen/join. Explicit disconnect starts120seconds grace directly. Idle30seconds only prompts; it never removes membership.

Once all but one player is ready, the final unready actor has5seconds. In rooms above2 the deadline removes only that actor and locks/starts the remaining countdown; exact2 retains both. Reads and actions can settle deadlines, so worker delay does not extend the policy.

Matrix API-joins every actor, navigates in waves of4, then sequentially waits for one live connection and readies that actor before checking the next. There is no all-pages-connected/full-roster barrier before the first ready. Thus the last readiness check may consume the5second holdout window that earlier ready actions created.

UI heartbeat requires loaded player role and open room; first interval attempt is20seconds after effect installation, not immediate. Presence acquires the current aggregate version under lock, preventing unrelated stale expectedVersion heartbeats from starving a valid actor. It cannot revive expired membership.

A valid guest session does not imply current room membership. Private UUID access rejects a nonmember with genericNOT_FOUND; the UI renders404 as room not found/invitation expired. Therefore a holdout removal can produce this screen without invalidating the guest session.
